stock.release: PyPI protenix 1.1.0 (uploaded 2026-03-23); the kit records the pip version, no upstream git commit

model_files.rule: sha256 of the installed module file (the members of stock/protenix-1.1.0-py3-none-any.whl): the stock files the big memory levers carry patched statements of (opt/protenix_v1_opt/big.py _module_pinned refuses a lever by name when the installed file differs)

pinned_stack.layernorm: LAYERNORM_TYPE=fast_layernorm (the stock fast LayerNorm extension; the kit installs its prebuilt stream-correct build of it)
pinned_stack.base: a CUDA 12.6 development userland with Python 3.11 (e.g. the nvidia/cuda:12.6.3-devel-ubuntu22.04 container image + python 3.11); nvcc runs once per box, only when the kit's prebuilt fast-LN .so does not match the stack (it rebuilds under TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR)
pinned_stack.install: pip install torch==2.7.1 torchvision==0.22.1 torchaudio==2.7.1 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126; pip install protenix==1.1.0 (== stock/protenix-1.1.0-py3-none-any.whl); then run.sh install (the shared core + this package, editable); environment LAYERNORM_TYPE=fast_layernorm PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 (configs/h100.env exports both)
pinned_stack.tested_on: the pinned stack: this base + install exactly (Python 3.11.5, torch 2.7.1+cu126, CUDA 12.6, triton 3.3.1, cuequivariance-torch 0.8.0) on H100 80GB — a documentation line: nothing reads or compares it

H100.note: the kit's reference class; the prebuilt stream-correct fast-LN .so (torch 2.13.0+cu130; sm_90 among its device code) loads as shipped on the tested stack, and is rebuilt from source with nvcc on another torch / CUDA

B200.note: the kit's Tier-1 rows exist on B200/B300; the stream-correct fast-LN is rebuilt from source there (nvcc)

A100.note: admitted by compute capability (any sm_80 card runs as this class, the 80 GB and the 40 GB card alike; a differing name is a NOTE; memory-dependent limits are read from the running device); 8.0 kernel rows are the shared core's cc-keyed tables and this kit's lib/fpf_trimul_v4/cells.json `8.0|3.3` / `8.0|*`; the prebuilt stream-correct fast-LN .so carries sm_80 device code and loads as shipped on the tested stack (rebuilt from source with nvcc on another torch / CUDA, as on every card)
